title: 描述东西的状态

examples.en: The soup is hot right now.
examples.zh: 汤现在很热。

examples.en: The pizza is ready at lunch.
examples.zh: 披萨午饭时好了。

examples.en: The bread is fresh today.
examples.zh: 面包今天很新鲜。

tipZh: 主语后面永远要有 is，不能像中文那样直接说“汤热”。形容词不变形，时间词放在句尾。

title: 汇报工作进度

examples.en: The proposal is waiting for approval at the moment.
examples.zh: 方案眼下正在等待批准。

examples.en: The budget is on track this week.
examples.zh: 预算本周进展顺利。

examples.en: The contract is under revision for now.
examples.zh: 合同目前正在修订中。

tipZh: “is + 介词短语/形容词短语”是汇报进度的万能句式，on hold、on track、under revision 都当作整块背。

title: 说明东西是谁的

examples.en: It is John's bag.
examples.zh: 它是约翰的包。

examples.en: That is my dad's umbrella.
examples.zh: 那是我爸爸的雨伞。

examples.en: This is Mary's phone.
examples.zh: 这是玛丽的手机。

tipZh: “某人的”直接在名字后加 's，后面的名词前不要再加 the 或 a。

title: 指出谁的重点是什么

examples.en: That is Sarah's main concern.
examples.zh: 那是萨拉的主要关注点。

examples.en: This is the company's key priority.
examples.zh: 这是公司的关键优先事项。

examples.en: It is our manager's current problem.
examples.zh: 这是我们经理的当前问题。

tipZh: 所有格 + 形容词 + 名词的顺序是固定的：先 's，再形容词，最后名词。

title: 把东西给某人

examples.en: I give John the keys every day.
examples.zh: 我每天给约翰钥匙。

examples.en: We send my sister the photos every week.
examples.zh: 我们每周寄给我姐姐照片。

examples.en: They bring the kids the tickets on weekends.
examples.zh: 他们周末带给孩子们票。

tipZh: 动词后面先放“人”，再放“东西”，中间不加 to。这个顺序和中文“给他一本书”是一样的。

title: 承诺把资料发给对方

options.en: by the end of the day

examples.en: I'll send the client the revised quote by Friday.
examples.zh: 我会在周五之前把修改后的报价单发给客户。

examples.en: We'll forward Sarah the signed contract as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 我们会尽快把签好的合同转发给萨拉。

examples.en: You'll email the manager the final report this afternoon.
examples.zh: 你会今天下午把最终报告用邮件发给经理。

tipZh: I'll / We'll 后面直接跟动词原形，再接“人 + 东西”。口语中 send、forward、email 都可以用这个结构。

title: 把东西给他/她/他们

examples.en: We give him the keys today.
examples.zh: 我们今天给他钥匙。

examples.en: I send them a gift on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我周日寄给他们一份礼物。

examples.en: You bring her the book every morning.
examples.zh: 你每天早上带给她书。

tipZh: 做宾语时代词要换格：he→him，she→her，they→them。宾格代词紧跟动词，后面再放东西。

title: 礼貌地请对方把东西给某人

examples.en: Please send me the agenda before the meeting.
examples.zh: 请在会议之前把议程发给我。

examples.en: Please forward them the draft as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 请尽快把草稿转发给他们。

examples.en: Please bring her the invoice this afternoon.
examples.zh: 请今天下午把发票带给她。

tipZh: Please + 动词原形是最安全的请求句式。人称代词一律用宾格：me、him、her、us、them。

title: 描述别人的日常习惯

examples.en: He gives it to John every morning.
examples.zh: 他每天早上把它给约翰。

examples.en: My brother brings the letter to my mother after lunch.
examples.zh: 我哥哥午饭后把那封信带给我妈妈。

examples.en: She hands the keys to the teacher at noon.
examples.zh: 她中午把钥匙交给老师。

tipZh: 主语是 he / she / 一个人名时，动词一定要加 -s。这个表里所有的主语都是第三人称单数，所以动词都带 -s。

title: 描述同事的工作习惯

options.en: at the end of the month

examples.en: Our manager reviews the report every Monday.
examples.zh: 我们经理每周一审阅报告。

examples.en: Sarah updates the schedule before each meeting.
examples.zh: 萨拉每次会议之前更新日程。

examples.en: The finance team approves the budget every quarter.
examples.zh: 财务团队每个季度批准预算。

tipZh: 谈论“习惯和常规”用一般现在时，主语是单数的人或团队时动词加 -s。团队名词（team）在这里当作单数。

title: 用代词说“把它给他”

examples.en: She gives it to him every day.
examples.zh: 她每天把它给他。

examples.en: My mom brings both of them to us every Monday.
examples.zh: 我妈妈每周一把它们两个带给我们。

examples.en: Tom sends it to her every week.
examples.zh: 汤姆每周把它寄给她。

tipZh: 东西和接收者都是代词时，永远是“it/them + to + 宾格代词”，不要说 gives him it。

title: 说明谁把东西交给谁

examples.en: Sarah forwards it to me before noon.
examples.zh: 萨拉在中午之前把它转发给我。

examples.en: The client submits all of them to us by the deadline.
examples.zh: 客户在截止日期前把它们全部提交给我们。

examples.en: My assistant delivers it to him on time.
examples.zh: 我的助理准时把它交付给他。

tipZh: 动词 + 代词宾语 + to + 宾格代词，是职场里转交文件最常用的句型。主语是单数时别忘了 -s。

title: 询问东西的状态

examples.en: Is the soup still hot?
examples.zh: 汤还热吗？

examples.en: Are the eggs really fresh?
examples.zh: 鸡蛋真的新鲜吗？

examples.en: Is your tea actually cold?
examples.zh: 你的茶到底凉吗？

tipZh: 一般疑问句把 is / are 提到句首：Is the soup hot? 副词 still / really / actually 放在主语之后、形容词之前。

title: 礼貌地询问能否做某事

options.en: by the end of the week

examples.en: Could you review the draft before the meeting?
examples.zh: 你能在会议之前审阅草稿吗？

examples.en: Can we send the invoice by tomorrow?
examples.zh: 我们能在明天之前发送发票吗？

examples.en: Will she update the contract this afternoon?
examples.zh: 她会今天下午更新合同吗？

tipZh: 情态动词提到主语前面就是问句，后面的动词永远用原形。Could you 比 Can you 更礼貌。
soundZh: Could you → Couldja；Can I → Can-nai（连读）

title: 描述多个东西

examples.en: The shoes are very new.
examples.zh: 鞋子非常新。

examples.en: The plates are pretty dirty.
examples.zh: 盘子挺脏。

examples.en: The windows are really clean.
examples.zh: 窗户真的很干净。

tipZh: 复数名词加 -s，be 动词用 are。形容词永远不变，只在 very / really 等程度词后面出现。

title: 汇报多项数据

examples.en: The sales figures are better than expected this quarter.
examples.zh: 销售数据本季度好于预期。

examples.en: The profit margins are lower than last year so far.
examples.zh: 利润率到目前为止低于去年。

examples.en: The survey results are very encouraging at the moment.
examples.zh: 调查结果目前非常令人鼓舞。

tipZh: figures、results、numbers、margins 都是复数，配 are。数据类名词在汇报里几乎总是复数。

title: 表达必须做的事

examples.en: I must pay the bill before dinner.
examples.zh: 我晚饭前必须付账单。

examples.en: We have to buy some milk tonight.
examples.zh: 我们今晚得买点牛奶。

examples.en: They should wash the car this weekend.
examples.zh: 他们这个周末应该洗车。

tipZh: must、should 后面直接接动词原形；have to、need to 的 to 是固定搭配，后面同样是原形。
soundZh: have to → hafta；need to → needa；should → shud（弱读）

title: 提醒必须完成的工作

options.en: by the end of the day

examples.en: I must submit the report by Friday.
examples.zh: 我在周五之前必须提交报告。

examples.en: We need to confirm the budget before the meeting.
examples.zh: 我们在会议之前需要确认预算。

examples.en: You should sign the contract ahead of the deadline.
examples.zh: 你在截止日期之前应该签署合同。

tipZh: must 最强硬，have to 强调外部要求，should 是建议。工作场合对同事多用 need to / should 更委婉。
soundZh: need to → needa；have to → hafta

title: 表达想做什么

examples.en: I want to cook dinner tonight.
examples.zh: 我想今晚做晚饭。

examples.en: He wants to take a walk after work.
examples.zh: 他想下班后散散步。

examples.en: I'd like to visit my grandma tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我很想明天去看望我奶奶。

tipZh: want 后面一定要加 to 再接动词原形。主语是 he / she 时用 wants，I'd like 比 I want 更礼貌。
soundZh: want to → wanna；I'd like to → I'd like-ta

title: 提出想谈的事

options.en: get your feedback on the draft

examples.en: I'd like to schedule a meeting with you this week.
examples.zh: 我想本周和你安排一次会议。

examples.en: The client wants to discuss the new proposal next month.
examples.zh: 客户想下个月讨论新的提案。

examples.en: We want to go over the budget as soon as possible.
examples.zh: 我们想尽快过一遍预算。

tipZh: 职场中 I'd like to ... 比 I want to ... 礼貌得多；第三人称用 wants to。
soundZh: I'd like to → I'd like-ta；want to → wanna

title: 说明接下来的打算

examples.en: I'm going to cook dinner tonight.
examples.zh: 我打算今晚做晚饭。

examples.en: They're going to watch a movie on Saturday.
examples.zh: 他们打算周六看场电影。

examples.en: She's going to go shopping next week.
examples.zh: 她打算下周去购物。

tipZh: be 动词随主语变化：I'm / he's / they're，后面的 going to 之后用动词原形。
soundZh: going to → gonna；I'm going to → I'm gonna

title: 宣布工作计划

options.en: before the end of the quarter
by the end of the year

examples.en: We're going to launch the new product next month.
examples.zh: 我们打算下个月推出新产品。

examples.en: She's going to hire two more developers early next week.
examples.zh: 她打算下周初再招两名开发人员。

examples.en: The team is going to present the results by the end of the year.
examples.zh: 团队打算在年底之前汇报结果。

tipZh: be going to 表示已有安排或计划。团队名词（The team）搭配 is，不是 are。
soundZh: going to → gonna

title: 表达不能做某事

examples.en: I can't eat the cake today.
examples.zh: 我今天不能吃蛋糕。

examples.en: They shouldn't drink the coffee tonight.
examples.zh: 他们今晚不应该喝咖啡。

examples.en: She won't drive the car this weekend.
examples.zh: 她这个周末不会开车。

tipZh: 情态动词的否定直接加 not（can't / won't / shouldn't），后面接动词原形，不要用 do。
soundZh: can't 的 t 常被吞掉，靠元音拉长来区别 can（弱读 /kən/）；shouldn't → shudn't

title: 委婉地拒绝或说明做不到

examples.en: We can't accept the offer until Friday.
examples.zh: 我们周五之前不能接受报价。

examples.en: I won't be able to approve the budget for now.
examples.zh: 我暂时无法批准预算。

examples.en: You don't need to share the files at this stage.
examples.zh: 你现阶段不需要分享文件。

tipZh: 拒绝时用 I won't be able to ... 比 I can't ... 更委婉；don't need to 表示“不必”，和 mustn't 不同。
soundZh: won't be able to → won't-be-able-ta；can't 的 t 常被吞掉

title: 说明已经做完的事

examples.en: I have already eaten lunch.
examples.zh: 我已经吃了午饭。

examples.en: She has finally finished the homework.
examples.zh: 她终于做完了作业。

examples.en: They have just paid the bill.
examples.zh: 他们刚刚付了账单。

tipZh: have / has + 过去分词。already、just、finally 放在 have 与过去分词之间；主语是 he / she 时用 has。
soundZh: I have → I've；she has → she's；have/has 弱读，几乎听不见

title: 汇报已经完成的工作

examples.en: We have already sent the invoice for the client.
examples.zh: 我们已经为客户发出了发票。

examples.en: The team has recently approved the budget for next quarter.
examples.zh: 团队最近为下个季度批准了预算。

examples.en: She has finally booked the venue for the launch.
examples.zh: 她终于为产品发布订好了场地。

tipZh: 现在完成时强调“已完成，与现在有关”，不要和 yesterday、last week 这类明确的过去时间连用。
soundZh: we have → we've；has → 's，弱读后很容易漏听

title: 汇报进度

options.en: sent the report to the client

examples.en: Good news, we've already booked the meeting room.
examples.zh: 好消息，我们已经订好了会议室。

examples.en: Just so you know, I've just sent the report to the client.
examples.zh: 跟你说一声，我刚刚把报告发给客户了。

examples.en: FYI, I've already fixed the bug.
examples.zh: 供你参考，我已经修好了这个漏洞。

tipZh: 汇报"已经做完"用现在完成时 have + 过去分词，重点是结果；already / just 放在 have 和过去分词之间。不要和 yesterday、last week 等明确的过去时间连用。
soundZh: I've already → I've-ahl-ready；we've → weev

title: 提出建议

examples.en: Why don't we split the work first thing tomorrow?
examples.zh: 我们明天一早把工作分一下，怎么样？

examples.en: Shall we go over the budget after lunch?
examples.zh: 我们午饭后过一遍预算，好吗？

examples.en: What if we set up a call on Monday?
examples.zh: 我们周一安排一次电话会议，可以吗？

tipZh: 四种句头都能接动词原形，语气从直接到委婉：Why don't we 最常用，Shall we 稍正式，What if we 更像试探。时间放在句尾。
soundZh: Why don't we → Why-don-we（t 吞音）；What if we → Whadif-we

title: 请对方说明

options.zh: 不好意思打断一下，不过

options.en: what you said about the budget
options.zh: 你说的关于预算的部分

examples.en: Sorry, I didn't catch the next step.
examples.zh: 不好意思，我没听清下一步。

examples.en: Excuse me, I'm not clear on what you just said.
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我不太清楚你刚才说的内容。

examples.en: Sorry to interrupt, but I'm not sure about the deadline you mentioned.
examples.zh: 不好意思打断一下，不过我不太确定你提到的截止日期。

tipZh: 没听懂时先说 Sorry 再坦白，比沉默或只说 "What?" 礼貌得多。didn't catch 指"没听清"，don't understand 指"没理解"，别混用。
soundZh: didn't catch → didn(t)-catch（t 吞音）；Sorry to → Sorry-ta

title: 约时间

examples.en: Hi, are you free tomorrow morning for a quick chat?
examples.zh: 你好，明天上午你有空聊几分钟吗？

examples.en: Quick question, are you available later today for a short call?
examples.zh: 问一下，今天晚些时候你方便通个电话吗？

examples.en: By the way, are you still free after the meeting to discuss the budget?
examples.zh: 对了，会议结束后你还有空讨论一下预算吗？

tipZh: 约时间用 Are you free / available + 时间，be 动词提到主语前面。free 更随意，available 更职场；时间放在形容词后面，不要加介词 at。
soundZh: are you free → Arya free

title: 请人转交

examples.en: Hi, could you send it to him today?
examples.zh: 你好，能不能今天把它发给他？

examples.en: Sorry, could you give them to her before lunch?
examples.zh: 抱歉，能不能午饭前把它们交给她？

examples.en: Excuse me, could you forward that to me as soon as you can?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，能不能尽快把那个转发给我？

tipZh: 物品是代词（it / them / that）时，必须先说物品再说 to + 人：send it to him，不能说 send him it。如果物品是名词，才可以说 send him the file。
soundZh: Could you → Couldja；send it to → sen-di-ta（it 与 to 连读）

title: 说明计划

options.en: by the end of the month

examples.en: We're planning to hire two more designers by the end of the month.
examples.zh: 我们打算月底前再招两名设计师。

examples.en: I'm hoping to book the venue early next quarter.
examples.zh: 我希望下个季度初订好场地。

examples.en: I'm planning to launch the new website next week.
examples.zh: 我打算下周上线新网站。

tipZh: be planning to / be hoping to 后面都接动词原形，比 I will 更委婉，适合向同事或上级说明还没完全确定的计划。be 动词要跟主语变化：I'm / We're。
soundZh: planning to → plannin'-ta；hoping to → hopin'-ta

title: 表达观点

examples.en: I think we should postpone the launch right away.
examples.zh: 我认为我们应该马上推迟发布。

examples.en: I don't think we can change the schedule this week.
examples.zh: 我不认为我们可以本周内调整日程。

examples.en: It seems to me that we have to talk to the client at the next meeting.
examples.zh: 在我看来我们必须在下次会议上和客户谈谈。

tipZh: 否定观点时英语习惯说 I don't think we should...，而不是 I think we shouldn't...。情态动词 should / can / have to 后面一律接动词原形。
soundZh: I think we should → I-think-we-shud；don't think → doan-think

title: 道歉并补救

examples.en: Sorry, I forgot to reply to your email. I'll do it right now.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我忘了回复你的邮件。我现在马上就去做。

examples.en: I'm so sorry, I didn't have time to finish the slides. I'll do it tonight.
examples.zh: 真的很抱歉，我没时间完成幻灯片。我今晚就去做。

examples.en: My apologies, I didn't get a chance to call the client. I'll do it first thing tomorrow.
examples.zh: 十分抱歉，我没来得及给客户打电话。我明天一早就去做。

tipZh: 道歉后一定要给出补救时间，这样才显得负责。过去没做的事用 didn't / wasn't able to + 动词原形；forgot to 后面也接原形。
soundZh: forgot to → forgotta；didn't get a chance to → didn' get-a chance-ta

title: 有条件的承诺

examples.en: Sure, if you send me the details, I'll start on it right away.
examples.zh: 没问题，如果你把详细资料发给我，我会马上着手处理。

examples.en: Don't worry, if the budget allows it, my manager will send you an update.
examples.zh: 别担心，如果预算允许，我的经理会给你发一份进展。

examples.en: OK, if everything goes well, we'll schedule a follow-up meeting.
examples.zh: 好的，如果一切顺利，我们会安排一次后续会议。

tipZh: if 从句用一般现在时（if the client agrees），主句才用 will，不要在 if 后面再加 will。send you an update 是双宾语结构：先说人，再说东西。

title: 表达偏好

examples.en: I'd rather meet in person than write a long email, if possible.
examples.zh: 如果可以的话，我宁愿当面谈，也不想写一封长邮件。

examples.en: We'd actually rather have a video call than wait for a reply, this time.
examples.zh: 这一次，我们其实宁愿开视频会议，也不想等对方回复。

examples.en: I'd actually rather talk on the phone than send lots of messages, for this project.
examples.zh: 在这个项目上，我其实宁愿打电话沟通，也不想发一堆消息。

tipZh: would rather 后面直接接动词原形（不加 to），than 后面也用原形：I'd rather meet than write。口语里 I'd 是 I would 的缩写，不是 I had。
soundZh: I'd rather → I'd-rather（'d 极弱）；rather than → rather-thn

title: 汇报未完成的工作

options.en: it should be ready by Friday
I'll send you a draft tomorrow
options.zh: 我明天给你发一份草稿

options.en: we've already finished the first part
options.zh: 我们已经完成了第一部分

options.en: we expect to finish next week

examples.en: Quick update, we're still working on the new design, but it should be ready by Friday.
examples.zh: 简单更新一下，我们还在处理新设计，不过周五前应该能完成。

examples.en: Right now, the team is still working on the client proposal, but I'll send you a draft tomorrow.
examples.zh: 现在，团队还在处理客户方案，不过我明天给你发一份草稿。

examples.en: As of now, I'm still working on the budget report, but we've already finished the first part.
examples.zh: 目前，我还在处理预算报告，不过我们已经完成了第一部分。

tipZh: 先说"还没完成"，再用 but 给出积极的进展，是职场汇报的好习惯。still 放在 be 动词之后、working 之前。第二个分句里的 it 指前面的工作。
soundZh: still working on → still workin' on

title: 委婉请求

options.en: I hate to bother you, but
options.zh: 实在不好意思打扰你，不过

options.en: giving me some feedback on my draft
introducing me to the new manager
if it's not too much trouble

examples.en: Sorry to ask, but would you mind sending me the slides when you have a moment?
examples.zh: 不好意思问一下，不过有空的时候能不能麻烦你把幻灯片发给我？

examples.en: I know you're busy, but would you mind introducing me to the new manager after the meeting?
examples.zh: 我知道你很忙，不过会议结束后能不能麻烦你把我介绍给新经理？

examples.en: I hate to bother you, but would you mind helping me with the report before you leave today?
examples.zh: 实在不好意思打扰你，不过今天下班前能不能麻烦你帮我处理一下报告？

tipZh: Would you mind 后面接动词 -ing，不是原形。想答应时说 "Not at all" 或 "Sure, no problem"（别说 Yes，Yes 会被理解为"介意"）。
soundZh: Would you mind → Wouldja mind

title: 说明要做的事

examples.en: I have to do the laundry after work.
examples.zh: 下班后我得洗衣服。

examples.en: I'd better call my mom tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 明天早上我最好给我妈妈打电话。

examples.en: I'm going to clean the kitchen before dinner.
examples.zh: 晚饭前我打算打扫厨房。

tipZh: 这一组开头词的力度不同：have to / need to 是必须做，I'd better 是"最好做，否则有麻烦"，I'm going to 是已经决定，I want to 是个人意愿。后面都接动词原形。
soundZh: have to → hafta；I'd better → I'd-better（better 的 t 变轻 d）；going to → gonna；want to → wanna

title: 请求许可

options.en: use your phone for a second

examples.en: Hey, can I sit here, if you don't mind?
examples.zh: 嘿，如果你不介意的话，我可以坐这里吗？

examples.en: Excuse me, can I borrow your charger, if it's no trouble?
examples.zh: 不好意思，如果不麻烦的话，我可以借一下你的充电器吗？

examples.en: Sorry, can I open the window, if possible?
examples.zh: 抱歉，如果方便的话，我可以开一下窗户吗？

tipZh: Can I... 是最常用的请求许可句型，朋友之间直接用；对陌生人在句尾加 if you don't mind 会更礼貌。借东西用 borrow（借入），不要和 lend（借出）弄混。
soundZh: Can I → Can-nai；if you don't mind → if-ya-doan-mind

title: 询问东西是谁的

examples.en: Excuse me, is that Tom's laptop in the kitchen?
examples.zh: 不好意思，厨房里那个是汤姆的笔记本电脑吗？

examples.en: By the way, is that your sister's bag by the door?
examples.zh: 对了，门边那个是你姐姐的包吗？

examples.en: Sorry, is that Anna's umbrella on the sofa?
examples.zh: 抱歉，沙发上那个是安娜的雨伞吗？

tipZh: 物主后面加 's 表示"……的"：Tom's laptop。问句要把 is 提到 that 前面（Is that...?）。如果物主是 your sister 这样的短语，'s 加在最后一个词上：your sister's bag。
soundZh: Is that → Izzat

title: 说明东西给了谁

examples.en: I gave it to her yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天把它交给了她。

examples.en: My sister lent them to him last week.
examples.zh: 我姐姐上周把它们借给了他。

examples.en: We passed that to you this morning.
examples.zh: 我们今天早上把那个递给了你。

tipZh: 宾语是代词时顺序固定：动词 + 物品 + to + 人（gave it to her）。不能说 gave her it。想用"人在前"的说法，物品必须是名词：gave her the book。

title: 谈没做过的事

options.zh: 不过我希望哪天能试一试
不过我真的很想试一试

options.en: and I don't really want to

options.zh: 不过我打算找机会试一试

examples.en: I've never tried sushi, but I'd love to.
examples.zh: 我从来没有尝过寿司，不过我很想试一试。

examples.en: I've still never been to Japan, but I'm planning to.
examples.zh: 我至今还没有去过日本，不过我打算找机会试一试。

examples.en: I've honestly never ridden a horse, and I don't really want to.
examples.zh: 说实话我从来没有骑过马，而且我也不太想试。

tipZh: I've never + 过去分词 表示"到现在为止从没有过"的经历，不加具体时间。注意不规则过去分词：been、ridden、seen。结尾的 to 后面省略了重复的动词。
soundZh: I've never → I've-never；I'd love to → I'd-love-ta

title: 评价物品

examples.en: I think these shoes are a bit small.
examples.zh: 我觉得这双鞋有点小。

examples.en: Honestly, this jacket is too expensive.
examples.zh: 说实话，这件夹克太贵了。

examples.en: Actually, these jeans are really comfortable.
examples.zh: 其实这条牛仔裤挺舒服的。

tipZh: this + 单数名词用 is，these + 复数名词用 are，be 动词要和名词的单复数一致。shoes、jeans 总是复数形式，所以用 these ... are。程度词 a bit / a little 修饰形容词时，不要加 very。

title: 有条件的计划

examples.en: We're going to visit my parents on Sunday, as long as nothing comes up.
examples.zh: 只要没有别的事，周日我们打算去看我父母。

examples.en: I'm probably going to go to the beach next Saturday, as long as the weather stays nice.
examples.zh: 只要天气一直不错，下周六我很可能会去海边。

examples.en: I'm going to go hiking tomorrow afternoon, as long as I feel better.
examples.zh: 只要我感觉好些了，明天下午我打算去爬山。

tipZh: be going to 表示已有打算，加 probably 语气变弱。as long as 后面的条件从句用一般现在时，不要写 will。时间可以放在 as long as 之前。
soundZh: going to → gonna；as long as → as-long-az

title: 描述别人的习惯

options.en: gets up at five every day

options.zh: 每个周末给家里打电话

examples.en: Actually, my neighbor cooks dinner every night, which I really admire.
examples.zh: 其实我邻居每天晚上做晚饭，这点我真的很佩服。

examples.en: You know, my boss gets up at five every day, which I find hard to believe.
examples.zh: 你知道吗，我老板每天五点起床，我觉得这难以置信。

examples.en: Honestly, my roommate works out before breakfast, which sometimes drives me crazy.
examples.zh: 说实话，我室友早饭前锻炼，这有时让我很抓狂。

tipZh: 主语是 he / she / my boss 这样的第三人称单数时，一般现在时的动词要加 -s（gets、works、cooks）。which 指代前面整件事，后面可以接评论。

title: 问路

examples.en: Excuse me, how can I get to the museum from here?
examples.zh: 不好意思，从这里怎么去博物馆？

examples.en: Pardon me, how can I get to the airport by subway?
examples.zh: 劳驾，坐地铁怎么去机场？

examples.en: Hi, how can I get to this address on foot?
examples.zh: 你好，步行怎么去这个地址？

tipZh: 问路先用 Excuse me 引起注意。how can I get to + 地点 是万能问法；交通方式用 by + 无冠词的交通工具（by bus），走路是 on foot。
soundZh: How can I → How-can-nai；get to → get-ta

title: 向前台提要求

options.en: extend my stay by one night
book a taxi for tomorrow morning
options.zh: 订一辆明天早上的出租车

options.en: if that's not too much trouble

examples.en: Good morning, I'd like to check out late, if possible.
examples.zh: 早上好，我想晚点退房，如果可以的话。

examples.en: Hi, I'd like to change my room, please.
examples.zh: 你好，我想换个房间，麻烦你了。

examples.en: Excuse me, I'd like to book a taxi for tomorrow morning, if that's OK with you.
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我想订一辆明天早上的出租车，如果你同意的话。

tipZh: I'd like to 比 I want to 礼貌得多，酒店、餐厅、柜台都适用，后面接动词原形。句尾加 please 或 if possible 能让语气更柔和。
soundZh: I'd like to → I'd like-ta

title: 购物问货

examples.en: Excuse me, do you have these shoes in a bigger size by any chance?
examples.zh: 不好意思，这双鞋你们碰巧有大一号的吗？

examples.en: Hi, do you have this shirt in black right now?
examples.zh: 你好，这件衬衫你们现在有黑色的吗？

examples.en: Sorry, do you have those jeans in a different color here?
examples.zh: 抱歉，那条牛仔裤你们这里有别的颜色的吗？

tipZh: 指示词要和商品的单复数一致：this jacket / these shoes。鞋、裤子这类成对的东西在英语里是复数（shoes、jeans）。问尺码用 in a bigger size，问颜色直接 in black。
soundZh: Do you have → Dya have；by any chance → by-any-chance（连读）

title: 反映问题
pattern: {opener} I think there's a problem with {thing}. Could you {request}?

options.en: talk to the manager about it

examples.en: Excuse me, I think there's a problem with my order. Could you check it for me?
examples.zh: 不好意思，我觉得我点的菜有问题。你能帮我查一下吗？

examples.en: Hi, I think there's a problem with the air conditioning. Could you talk to the manager about it?
examples.zh: 你好，我觉得空调有问题。你能和经理说一下吗？

examples.en: Sorry, I think there's a problem with the bill. Could you take a look at it?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我觉得账单有问题。你能看一下吗？

tipZh: 先用 I think there's a problem with... 客观地说出问题，不要直接指责对方，再用 Could you... 提出请求。it 指代前面提到的东西，me 是宾格，不能写成 I。
soundZh: there's a → there-za；Could you → Couldja

title: 礼貌地打听信息

options.en: where I can buy a ticket
which platform the train leaves from
how long it takes to get there

examples.en: Excuse me, I'm a bit lost, so could you tell me where I can buy a ticket?
examples.zh: 不好意思，我有点迷路了，你能告诉我我在哪里可以买票吗？

examples.en: Hi, I'm in a hurry, so could you tell me which platform the train leaves from?
examples.zh: 你好，我很赶时间，你能告诉我火车从哪个站台出发吗？

examples.en: Pardon me, I'm just visiting, so could you tell me what time the museum opens?
examples.zh: 劳驾，我只是来旅游的，你能告诉我博物馆几点开门吗？

tipZh: 嵌入式问句里不再倒装：说 where I can buy a ticket，不说 where can I buy a ticket。只有外层的 Could you 才倒装。先说明自己的处境，对方更愿意帮忙。
soundZh: Could you tell me → Couldja tell me

title: 问对方的经历

examples.en: By the way, have you ever been to Japan before?
examples.zh: 对了，你以前去过日本吗？

examples.en: Hey, have you ever met a famous person yourself?
examples.zh: 嘿，你自己见过名人吗？

examples.en: Out of curiosity, have you ever seen the northern lights by any chance?
examples.zh: 我有点好奇，你碰巧看过北极光吗？

tipZh: Have you ever + 过去分词? 是聊天破冰的经典问法，问的是"有没有这种经历"，不说具体时间。回答用 Yes, I have. / No, never. 追问细节时才改用一般过去时。
soundZh: Have you ever → Havya-ever

title: 发出邀请

examples.en: Hey, do you want to grab a bite after work?
examples.zh: 嘿，下班后想不想吃点东西？

examples.en: So, do you want to watch a movie this weekend?
examples.zh: 那，这个周末想不想看场电影？

examples.en: Hi, do you want to hang out sometime next week?
examples.zh: 嗨，下周找个时间想不想一起玩？

tipZh: Do you want to...? 是朋友间最自然的邀请。比它更随意的是 Wanna...?，更礼貌的是 Would you like to...?。助动词 do 放在主语 you 之前，want 后面的动词用原形。
soundZh: Do you want to → Dya wanna

title: 分享一直想做的事

options.en: but I've never had the chance
but I've never found the time
but I've never been able to
and this year I'm finally going to
options.zh: 而且今年我终于打算去做了

examples.en: Me too, I've always wanted to learn to play the guitar, but I've never found the time.
examples.zh: 我也是，我一直想学弹吉他，但是一直没有时间。

examples.en: Wow, I've always wanted to run a marathon, and this year I'm finally going to.
examples.zh: 哇，我一直想跑一次马拉松，而且今年我终于打算去做了。

examples.en: Honestly, I've always wanted to live by the sea, but I've never had the chance.
examples.zh: 说实话，我一直想住在海边，但是一直没有机会。

tipZh: I've always wanted to + 动词原形，用现在完成时表示"从以前一直到现在都想"。后半句常用 but I've never... 说明还没实现的原因。
soundZh: I've always wanted to → I've always wanted-ta

title: 婉拒邀请
pattern: {opener} I can't make it to {owner}'s {event} {time}, because {reason}.

examples.en: Unfortunately, I can't make it to Anna's wedding tomorrow night, because I have an early flight.
examples.zh: 很遗憾，明晚我没办法参加安娜的婚礼，因为我有一趟早班飞机。

examples.en: I'd love to, but I can't make it to my boss's farewell party this Friday, because I have to work late.
examples.zh: 我很想去，不过这个周五我没办法参加我老板的欢送会，因为我得加班。

examples.en: Thanks for the invitation, but I can't make it to Tom's housewarming on Saturday, because I'm visiting my parents.
examples.zh: 谢谢邀请，不过周六我没办法参加汤姆的乔迁派对，因为我要去看我父母。

tipZh: 拒绝邀请的公式：先感谢或表示遗憾，再说 I can't make it，最后简短给出理由。can't 后面接动词原形；owner's 表示"某人的"活动，名字或名词后加 's。
soundZh: can't make it → can't-make-it（make it 连读成 makit）

title: 转述别人的看法

examples.en: Apparently, my neighbor thinks that we should leave early.
examples.zh: 听说我邻居认为我们应该早点出发。

examples.en: By the way, my friend mentioned that it's going to rain tomorrow.
examples.zh: 对了，我朋友提到明天会下雨。

examples.en: Well, my sister told me that this restaurant is really good.
examples.zh: 嗯，我姐姐告诉我这家餐厅真的很棒。

tipZh: 转述一次具体的话用过去式（said / told me / mentioned）；转述对方一贯的看法用一般现在时，第三人称单数动词要加 -s（my friend thinks）。口语里不必严格改时态，that 也常可省略。

title: 请教怎么说

examples.en: Excuse me, how do you say this word in English?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，这个词用英语怎么说？

examples.en: Teacher, how do you spell that word in English?
examples.zh: 老师，那个词用英语怎么拼？

examples.en: Quick question, how do you pronounce this new word in English?
examples.zh: 问一下，这个新词用英语怎么读？

tipZh: How do you say X in English? 是学英语最有用的一句，无论词汇多少都能靠它继续对话。how 后面用 do you 倒装，动词用原形。
soundZh: how do you → how-d'ya

title: 说明学习目标

examples.en: I want to improve my speaking by taking an online class.
examples.zh: 我想通过上网课来提高口语。

examples.en: I'm trying to improve my vocabulary by practicing every day.
examples.zh: 我正在努力通过每天练习来提高词汇量。

examples.en: I'm hoping to improve my pronunciation by talking to native speakers.
examples.zh: 我希望通过和母语者交流来提高发音。

tipZh: want to / need to / hope to 后面接动词原形；by 是介词，后面必须接 -ing 形式（by practicing），不能接原形。
soundZh: want to → wanna；trying to → tryin'-ta

title: 倾诉学习困难
pattern: {opener} I've been studying {language} for {duration}, but I still {problem}.

examples.en: Honestly, I've been studying Spanish for two years, but I still can't follow fast speech.
examples.zh: 说实话，我学西班牙语已经两年了，但我还是跟不上快速的对话。

examples.en: The thing is, I've been studying English for a long time, but I still get nervous when I speak.
examples.zh: 问题是，我学英语已经很长时间了，但我还是一说话就紧张。

examples.en: To be honest, I've been studying French for about three weeks, but I still forget new words quickly.
examples.zh: 老实说，我学法语已经三周左右了，但我还是很快就忘记新单词。

tipZh: I've been studying ... for + 一段时间，表示从过去持续到现在的动作；for 后面接时间长度（two years），since 后面才接起点。still 放在主语之后、动词之前。
soundZh: I've been → I've-bin（been 弱读）

title: 向老师求助
pattern: {opener} I'm having trouble with {topic} because {reason}. Could you {request}?
patternZh: {opener}我在{topic}上遇到了困难，因为{reason}。你能{request}吗？

options.en: I keep making the same mistakes
I can never remember the rules

examples.en: Teacher, I'm having trouble with the past tense because I don't get enough practice. Could you give me some tips?
examples.zh: 老师，我在过去时上遇到了困难，因为我练习得不够。你能给我一些建议吗？

examples.en: Sorry, I'm having trouble with this exercise because I get confused easily. Could you explain that again?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我在这个练习上遇到了困难，因为我很容易搞混。你能再解释一遍吗？

examples.en: Honestly, I'm having trouble with phrasal verbs because I keep making the same mistakes. Could you give me an example?
examples.zh: 说实话，我在短语动词上遇到了困难，因为我总是犯同样的错误。你能给我举个例子吗？

tipZh: have trouble with + 名词 表示"在……上有困难"。give me an example 是双宾语结构：先说人（me），再说东西（an example）；人是代词时要用宾格 me，不能用 I。
soundZh: Could you → Couldja

title: 表达心情

examples.en: I'm so nervous about the interview.
examples.zh: 我对这次面试特别紧张。

examples.en: We're pretty excited about the trip.
examples.zh: 我们对这次旅行挺兴奋。

examples.en: She's a bit worried about the results.
examples.zh: 她对结果有点担心。

tipZh: 表达心情用 be + 形容词 + about + 引起心情的事。be 动词不能省（不能说 I so nervous），程度词 so / really / a bit / pretty 放在形容词前面。

title: 说明原因

examples.en: Sorry, I left early because I was exhausted.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我提前走了，因为我累坏了。

examples.en: Honestly, I took a taxi because the weather was awful.
examples.zh: 说实话，我打车了，因为天气太糟了。

examples.en: Well, I skipped the gym because I wasn't feeling well.
examples.zh: 嗯，我没去健身房，因为我觉得不舒服。

tipZh: 先说结果，再用 because 说原因：结果 + because + 完整的句子（主语 + 动词）。不要像中文那样把 because 后面的句子省掉主语。
soundZh: because → 'cause（口语常缩成 cuz）

title: 问对方过去做过什么

examples.en: So, did you watch the match yesterday?
examples.zh: 那，你昨天看比赛了吗？

examples.en: By the way, did you call your mom this morning?
examples.zh: 对了，你今天早上给你妈妈打电话了吗？

examples.en: Hey, did you go to the gym on Sunday?
examples.zh: 嘿，你周日去健身房了吗？

tipZh: 问过去的事用 Did you + 动词原形：Did you go，不是 Did you went。时间词 yesterday / last night 等放在句尾，且要用过去的时间，不能和 have 连用。
soundZh: did you → didja

title: 主动提出帮忙

examples.en: Would you like me to carry that for you?
examples.zh: 你想让我替你拿那个吗？

examples.en: Do you need me to call a taxi before you go?
examples.zh: 需要我在你走之前叫辆出租车吗？

examples.en: Can I turn the heat up later?
examples.zh: 我可以待会儿把暖气调高吗？

tipZh: Would you like me to / Do you want me to 后面接动词原形（不加 to）：Would you like me to call a taxi? 主动帮忙时用这几个句头最自然，Can I 更随意。
soundZh: Would you like me to → Wouldja like me-ta；Do you want me to → Dya want me-ta

title: 点餐

examples.en: Can I have the burger and a cola, to go?
examples.zh: 我想点汉堡和一杯可乐，外带。

examples.en: Could I have the pasta and an iced tea, please?
examples.zh: 我想要意面和一杯冰茶，麻烦了。

examples.en: Could I get the soup of the day and a glass of water, for here?
examples.zh: 我想来今日例汤和一杯水，在这里吃。

tipZh: Can I have / Could I get 是点餐万能开头，比 I want 礼貌得多。to go 是外带（英国多说 to take away），for here 是堂食。饮料前别忘了 a / an。
soundZh: Can I have → Can-nai-have；Could I get → Could-dai-get

title: 说明会需要什么

examples.en: I'm going to need a haircut for the interview.
examples.zh: 为了这次面试，我会需要剪个头发。

examples.en: You're going to need a lot of help for the trip.
examples.zh: 为了这次旅行，你会需要很多帮助。

examples.en: I'm probably going to need a good night's sleep for the wedding.
examples.zh: 为了婚礼，我很可能会需要好好睡一觉。

tipZh: I'm going to need … 表示“到时候我会需要……”，比直接说 I need 更有预见感。need 后面接名词，不是动词：need a haircut；for + 事件说明用途。
soundZh: going to need → gonna need

title: 向医生说明症状

examples.en: Doctor, I've had a fever since Monday.
examples.zh: 医生，我从周一起一直发烧。

examples.en: Excuse me, I've had a bad cough since last night.
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我从昨晚起一直咳得厉害。

examples.en: Well, I've had a stomachache since the weekend.
examples.zh: 嗯，我从周末起一直胃疼。

tipZh: 症状持续到现在，用现在完成时 I've had …，再用 since + 起点（昨天、周一）。如果说一段时间则用 for：for three days。症状名词前通常要加 a。
soundZh: I've had → I've-had

title: 请人帮忙解决设备问题

options.en: Could you take a look at it
Do you know how to fix it
Could you show me how to reset it

examples.en: Excuse me, my laptop won't turn on. Could you take a look at it?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我的笔记本电脑开不了机。你能帮我看一下吗？

examples.en: Sorry, my phone can't connect to the Wi-Fi. Could you show me how to reset it?
examples.zh: 不好意思，我的手机连不上无线网。你能教我怎么重置吗？

examples.en: Hi, my printer isn't working properly. Do you know how to fix it?
examples.zh: 你好，我的打印机运转不正常。你知道怎么修吗？

tipZh: 描述设备坏了：won't + 动词原形（won't turn on）表示“怎么也打不开”，can't connect 表示“连不上”。my 后面不要再加 the。请求帮助用 Could you … 更礼貌。
soundZh: won't turn on → wont-turn-on；Do you know how to → Dya know how-ta

title: 询问数量

examples.en: How many people do we need for the party?
examples.zh: 派对我们需要多少人？

examples.en: How much money will we need in total?
examples.zh: 总共我们会需要多少钱？

examples.en: How many days do you think we'll need for the trip?
examples.zh: 这次旅行你觉得我们会需要多少天？

tipZh: 可数名词（people、bags、days）用 How many，不可数名词（time、money）用 How much。疑问句里助动词放在主语前面：How much time do we need，不是 we need。
soundZh: do we need → d'we need；do you think we'll → d'ya think we'll

title: 预约或改约

options.en: book an appointment for Friday afternoon
reschedule my appointment to next week
confirm my appointment for Monday morning
change my appointment to a later time

examples.en: Hello, I'd like to book an appointment for Friday afternoon, please.
examples.zh: 你好，我想预约周五下午的号，麻烦了。

examples.en: Good morning, I'd like to reschedule my appointment to next week, if possible.
examples.zh: 早上好，我想把预约改到下周，如果可以的话。

examples.en: Hi there, I'd like to cancel my appointment for tomorrow, if that's okay.
examples.zh: 你好呀，我想取消明天的预约，如果你方便的话。

tipZh: I'd like to + 动词原形 是电话预约、改约时最礼貌的开头。appointment 指与医生、律师、理发师等的预约；餐厅订位说 reservation。
soundZh: I'd like to → I'd like-ta

title: 比较两样东西

examples.en: This one is much cheaper than I expected.
examples.zh: 这个比我预想的便宜得多。

examples.en: The new one is a bit easier than the old one.
examples.zh: 新的比旧的容易一点。

examples.en: Mine is slightly better than I thought.
examples.zh: 我的比我想的好一点点。

tipZh: 比较级 + than：cheaper than、better than、more … than。程度词放在比较级前面：much / a lot / a bit / slightly cheaper，不要放在 than 后面。than I expected 是“比我预想的”常用说法。

title: 谈过去的习惯

options.en: when I was in high school

examples.en: Believe it or not, I used to play football when I was a kid.
examples.zh: 说来你可能不信，我小时候常常踢足球。

examples.en: Actually, I used to stay up until midnight when I was young.
examples.zh: 其实，我年轻的时候常常熬夜到半夜。

examples.en: Honestly, I used to walk to school when I was in high school.
examples.zh: 说实话，我上高中的时候常常走路上学。

tipZh: used to + 动词原形 说“过去经常……，现在不了”，to 后面是原形，不要写成 used to played。否定和疑问用 didn’t use to / Did you use to。
soundZh: used to → useta

title: 预测将来

examples.en: I think it'll rain tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我觉得明天会下雨。

examples.en: I bet the traffic will be terrible this weekend.
examples.zh: 我敢打赌这个周末路上会很堵。

examples.en: I'm pretty sure the weather will get better by tonight.
examples.zh: 我很确定到今晚天气会好起来。

tipZh: 预测将来用 will（常缩写成 it'll）：I think + 句子，that 可以省略。语气从弱到强：I guess < I think < I'm pretty sure。时间词放在句尾。
soundZh: it'll → ittle；I bet → I-bet

title: 给对方建议

examples.en: Honestly, if I were you, I'd see a doctor first.
examples.zh: 说实话，如果我是你，我会先去看医生。

examples.en: Personally, if I were you, I'd take a few days off right away.
examples.zh: 我个人觉得，如果我是你，我会马上休息几天。

examples.en: Look, if I were you, I'd call the bank before doing anything else.
examples.zh: 听我说，如果我是你，我会在做别的事之前先给银行打个电话。

tipZh: If I were you, I'd … 是给建议的经典句式，假设语气里 if 后面用 were（不是 was）。后面接动词原形。比 You should 更委婉，不会显得在命令别人。
soundZh: If I were you, I'd → If-I-wer-ya, I'd

title: 打电话找人
pattern: Hello, this is {name} from {company}. Could I speak to {person}, please?
patternZh: 你好，我是{company}的{name}。请问我可以和{person}通话吗？

options.en: the person in charge of billing

examples.en: Hello, this is Anna from the Shanghai office. Could I speak to Mr. Brown, please?
examples.zh: 你好，我是上海办公室的安娜。请问我可以和布朗先生通话吗？

examples.en: Hello, this is Tom Lee from the sales team. Could I speak to someone in accounting, please?
examples.zh: 你好，我是销售团队的汤姆·李。请问我可以和会计部的人通话吗？

examples.en: Hello, this is Linda Wu from ABC Logistics. Could I speak to the person in charge of billing, please?
examples.zh: 你好，我是ABC物流的琳达·吴。请问我可以和负责账单的人通话吗？

tipZh: 电话里自报家门用 This is …（不说 I am …），找人用 Could I speak to …?。找不到具体的人时，可以说 someone in + 部门 / the person in charge of + 事情。
soundZh: Could I → Could-dai；this is → this-iz

title: 写邮件说明来意

options.en: let you know about a delay
Please let me know if you have any questions
options.zh: 如有任何问题，请告诉我

options.en: Thanks in advance for your help
I look forward to hearing from you
Please reply when you get a chance

examples.en: Hi Anna, I'm writing to follow up on our meeting. Please let me know if you have any questions.
examples.zh: 安娜你好，我写这封邮件是想跟进一下我们的会议。如有任何问题，请告诉我。

examples.en: Dear Mr. Lee, I'm writing to ask about the invoice. Please reply when you get a chance.
examples.zh: 尊敬的李先生，我写这封邮件是想询问发票的事。方便时请回复我。

examples.en: Hello team, I'm writing to let you know about a delay. Thanks in advance for your help.
examples.zh: 大家好，我写这封邮件是想通知你们有一处延误。先谢谢你的帮助。

tipZh: I'm writing to + 动词原形 是邮件开头点明来意的固定说法，to 后面不要加 for。结尾一句要跟着来意走，Please let me know … 和 I look forward to … 最常用。
soundZh: I'm writing to → I'm writin'-ta

title: 说明操作步骤
pattern: {opener} first, you need to {first}. Then, you can {then}.
patternZh: {opener}首先，你需要{first}。然后，你就可以{then}了。

examples.en: Sure, it's simple: first, you need to log in to the system. Then, you can upload your file.
examples.zh: 当然，很简单：首先，你需要登录系统。然后，你就可以上传文件了。

examples.en: Okay, here's how it works: first, you need to fill out the form. Then, you can submit the request.
examples.zh: 好的，流程是这样的：首先，你需要填写表格。然后，你就可以提交申请了。

examples.en: It's easy: first, you need to set up your account. Then, you can choose your team.
examples.zh: 很容易：首先，你需要设置好你的账号。然后，你就可以选择你的团队了。

tipZh: First … Then … 让步骤一目了然。需要先完成的事用 you need to，完成之后才可以做的事用 you can。后面都接动词原形。
soundZh: need to → needa

title: 通知安排有变

options.en: the meeting has been moved to
the deadline has been extended to
the launch has been postponed to
the call has been rescheduled to
the review has been pushed back to
Let me know if that's a problem

examples.en: FYI, the meeting has been moved to Friday morning. Sorry for the late notice.
examples.zh: 供你参考：会议已经改到周五上午。抱歉通知得这么晚。

examples.en: Please note that the call has been rescheduled to 3 p.m. tomorrow. Hope that works for everyone.
examples.zh: 请注意，电话会议已经改期到明天下午三点。希望对大家都合适。

examples.en: Quick update: the deadline has been extended to the end of the month. Please update your calendar.
examples.zh: 最新消息：截止日期已经延长到月底。请更新一下你的日历。

tipZh: has been + 过去分词 是被动语态的现在完成时，强调“已经改了”，不必说是谁改的。后面的 to + 新时间 说明改到什么时候。
soundZh: has been moved → has-bin-moved（been 弱读）

title: 解释为什么没能及时处理

options.en: take my son to the doctor
help a colleague with a report

examples.en: Sorry, I had to deal with an urgent problem yesterday, so I missed your call.
examples.zh: 抱歉，昨天我得处理一个紧急问题，所以我错过了你的电话。

examples.en: Apologies, I had to take my son to the doctor last night, so I'm running a bit behind.
examples.zh: 十分抱歉，昨晚我得带儿子去看医生，所以我进度有点落后。

examples.en: Sorry again, I had to help a colleague with a report this morning, so I couldn't reply earlier.
examples.zh: 再次抱歉，今天早上我得帮同事处理一份报告，所以我没能早点回复。

tipZh: had to 是 have to 的过去式，表示“当时不得不……”，后面接动词原形。先说原因（I had to …），再用 so 带出结果，比单纯说 Sorry 更有说服力。
soundZh: had to → hadta

title: 礼貌地表示不同意

examples.en: I see what you mean, but that won't work for now.
examples.zh: 我明白你的意思，但目前那行不通。

examples.en: I understand your concern, but we shouldn't rush into it at this stage.
examples.zh: 我理解你的顾虑，但现阶段我们不应该操之过急。

examples.en: You may be right, but we can't commit to that right now.
examples.zh: 你可能是对的，但现在我们没法答应下来。

tipZh: 先认同、再用 but 提出不同意见，是职场里最不伤人的说法。for now / right now / at this stage 把反对限定在“现在”，给对方留面子。
soundZh: I see what you mean → I see whatcha mean；that won't → that-wont

title: 委婉地提出协商

options.en: I know it's a lot, but
move the deadline back a week

options.zh: 把我们的电话会议改到周五

options.en: extend the contract by a month
if that's not too much trouble

examples.en: Sorry to ask, but would it be possible to move the deadline back a week if that's not too much trouble?
examples.zh: 不好意思问一下，不过如果不太麻烦的话，有没有可能把截止日期延后一周？

examples.en: I know it's a lot, but would it be possible to get a small discount just this once?
examples.zh: 我知道要求有点多，但就这一次，有没有可能拿到一点小折扣？

examples.en: Hi there, would it be possible to have a little more time given the circumstances?
examples.zh: 你好，考虑到目前的情况，有没有可能多给我们一点时间？

tipZh: Would it be possible to + 动词原形 是协商、争取让步时最常用的委婉句式，比 Can you 客气得多。句尾加 just this once 之类的缓和语，更容易被接受。
soundZh: Would it be → Woulditbe（连读）

title: 确认自己的理解

examples.en: So what you're saying is that we need more time, is that right?
examples.zh: 所以，你的意思是我们需要更多时间，是这样吗？

examples.en: Just to be clear, what you're saying is that the launch will be delayed, did I get that right?
examples.zh: 为了确认一下，你的意思是发布会被推迟，我理解对了吗？

examples.en: Okay, so what you're saying is that you'd like to start over, am I right?
examples.zh: 好的，所以你的意思是你想重新开始，我说得对吗？

tipZh: 复述对方的话来确认理解：what you’re saying is that + 完整句子。末尾的确认问句要用倒装：is that right / did I get that right，不能说 that is right?。
soundZh: what you're saying → whatcher saying；did I get that right → didn-I-get-that-right

title: 递上对方要的东西

options.en: Let me know what you think
Take a look when you can

examples.en: Sure, here's the report that I told you about. Hope that helps.
examples.zh: 当然，这是我跟你提过的报告。希望有帮助。

examples.en: Okay, here's the link that you asked me for. Let me know what you think.
examples.zh: 好的，这是你向我要的链接。看完告诉我你的想法。

examples.en: Of course, here's the file that I showed you yesterday. Take a look when you can.
examples.zh: 当然可以，这是我昨天给你看过的文件。有空时看一下。

tipZh: 用 that 引导定语从句来说明“哪一个”：the report that I told you about。从句里的 that 指的是宾语，常常可以省略：the report I told you about。
soundZh: here's the → here-zthe；told you → told-ya

title: 不确定但答应查清楚
pattern: {opener} I'm not sure {clause}, but I'll check and let you know {time}.
patternZh: {opener}我不确定{clause}，但我会查一下，{time}告诉你。

examples.en: Honestly, I'm not sure where the file is, but I'll check and let you know later today.
examples.zh: 说实话，我不确定文件在哪儿，但我会查一下，今天晚些时候告诉你。

examples.en: Sorry, I'm not sure how much it costs, but I'll check and let you know as soon as I can.
examples.zh: 抱歉，我不确定要花多少钱，但我会查一下，一有消息就告诉你。

examples.en: To be honest, I'm not sure what time the office closes, but I'll check and let you know first thing tomorrow.
examples.zh: 老实说，我不确定办公室几点关门，但我会查一下，明天一早告诉你。

tipZh: I'm not sure + 疑问词 + 陈述语序：I’m not sure where the file is，不是 where is the file。I'll check and let you know 是不知道答案时的体面回答。
soundZh: let you know → letcha know；I'm not sure → I'm not-sure

title: 询问附近有没有某地

examples.en: Excuse me, is there a pharmacy near here?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，这附近有药店吗？

examples.en: Sorry, is there an ATM in this area?
examples.zh: 不好意思，这个区域有取款机吗？

examples.en: Quick question, is there a public restroom nearby?
examples.zh: 请问一下，附近有公共厕所吗？

tipZh: Is there + a / an + 单数名词 问“有没有”，注意 a pharmacy / an ATM 的 a / an。复数用 Are there any …?。near here 和 around here 都是“这附近”。
soundZh: is there a → is-there-a

title: 告诉别人某地在哪

options.en: at the end of this street

examples.en: Sure, the pharmacy is next to the bank.
examples.zh: 好的，药店就在银行旁边。

examples.en: Yes, the bus stop is across from the station.
examples.zh: 有的，公交站就在车站对面。

examples.en: Oh, the post office is behind the hotel.
examples.zh: 哦，邮局就在酒店后面。

tipZh: 说位置用 be + 介词短语：is next to / is across from / is behind。next to = 紧挨着，across from = 在对面，around the corner = 拐个弯就到。

title: 问班次时间

examples.en: Excuse me, what time does the last train leave tomorrow?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，明天末班火车几点出发？

examples.en: Sorry, what time does the first bus arrive on Sundays?
examples.zh: 不好意思，周日首班公交几点到达？

examples.en: Quick question, what time does the airport shuttle get here on weekdays?
examples.zh: 问一下，工作日机场大巴几点到这儿？

tipZh: What time does + 主语 + 动词原形？助动词 does 已经带了第三人称 -s，所以后面是 leave，不是 leaves。arrive / leave / depart 是班次时间最常用的三个动词。
soundZh: what time does → whaddime-duz

title: 请人推荐

examples.en: Excuse me, can you recommend a good restaurant near here?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，这附近你能推荐一家不错的餐厅吗？

examples.en: Hi, could you recommend a good dentist around here?
examples.zh: 你好，这一带你可以推荐一位不错的牙医吗？

examples.en: By the way, would you recommend a good bookstore in this area?
examples.zh: 对了，这个区域你会推荐一家不错的书店吗？

tipZh: recommend 后面直接跟名词：recommend a good restaurant，不用 to。Do you happen to know … 语气更随意，像是“碰巧你知道的话”。
soundZh: can you → kenya；do you happen to know → dya happen-ta know

title: 问路程要多久
pattern: {opener} how long does it take to get to {place} {mode}?

examples.en: Excuse me, how long does it take to get to the airport by bus?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，从这里坐公交到机场要多长时间？

examples.en: Sorry, how long does it take to get to the beach on foot?
examples.zh: 不好意思，从这里步行到海滩要多长时间？

examples.en: Quick question, how long does it take to get to the old town by taxi?
examples.zh: 问一下，从这里打车到老城区要多长时间？

tipZh: How long does it take to + 动词原形 问“要花多长时间”，it 是固定的形式主语。交通方式用 by + 无冠词名词（by bus），步行说 on foot。
soundZh: how long does it take → how-long-duzit-take

title: 买车票

examples.en: Hi, I'd like a one-way ticket to Boston for Friday, please.
examples.zh: 你好，我想买周五去波士顿的一张单程票，麻烦了。

examples.en: Excuse me, I'd like two round-trip tickets to Paris for tomorrow morning, please.
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我想买明天早上去巴黎的两张往返票，麻烦了。

examples.en: Good morning, I'd like two adult tickets to Central Station for the next departure, please.
examples.zh: 早上好，我想买下一班去中央车站的两张成人票，麻烦了。

tipZh: I'd like + 名词 是买票、点东西的礼貌说法。one-way = 单程（英式说 single），round-trip = 往返（英式说 return）。票数和 ticket 的单复数要一致。

title: 说明东西落在哪了
pattern: {opener} I think I've left {thing} in {place}. Could you {request}?

options.en: call me if you find it
options.zh: 在找到后给我打个电话

options.en: ask the staff to look for it
options.zh: 让工作人员帮忙找一找

options.en: keep it for me until tomorrow

examples.en: Excuse me, I think I've left my passport in the taxi. Could you check the lost and found?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，我好像把护照落在出租车上了。你能查一下失物招领处吗？

examples.en: Sorry to bother you, I think I've left my phone in the restaurant. Could you call me if you find it?
examples.zh: 不好意思打扰一下，我好像把手机落在餐厅里了。你能在找到后给我打个电话吗？

examples.en: Hello, I think I've left my jacket in the shop. Could you keep it for me until tomorrow?
examples.zh: 您好，我好像把外套落在店里了。你能替我保管到明天吗？

tipZh: leave 的过去分词是 left：I've left my phone in the taxi。I think 让语气更不肯定、更礼貌。忘带用 leave，丢了用 lose：I've lost my wallet。
soundZh: I've left → I've-left；Could you → Couldja

title: 寒暄问近况

examples.en: Hey, how's your new job going so far?
examples.zh: 嘿，到目前为止你的新工作怎么样了？

examples.en: Hi there, how's the move going this week?
examples.zh: 你好呀，这周搬家的事怎么样了？

examples.en: By the way, how's the renovation going lately?
examples.zh: 对了，最近装修怎么样了？

tipZh: How's + 事情 + going? 是关心别人近况的万能问法，how's 是 how is 的缩写。不要说 How is your job going on。
soundZh: how's → howz；going → goin'

title: 感谢并说明原因

examples.en: Thanks so much for helping me move last night.
examples.zh: 非常感谢你昨晚帮我搬家。

examples.en: Thank you so much for lending me your charger yesterday.
examples.zh: 真的很感谢你昨天借我充电器。

examples.en: Thanks a lot for waiting for me today.
examples.zh: 谢谢你今天等我。

tipZh: 感谢的原因放在 for 后面，动词要用 -ing 形式：Thanks for helping me，不是 Thanks for help me。me 是宾语，不能说 helping I。
soundZh: Thanks so much for → Thanks-so-much-fer

title: 夸奖别人

examples.en: Wow, I really like your jacket.
examples.zh: 哇，我真的很喜欢你的外套。

examples.en: By the way, I absolutely love your handwriting.
examples.zh: 对了，我超级喜欢你的字。

examples.en: Honestly, I'm crazy about your cooking.
examples.zh: 说实话，我特别喜欢你做的菜。

tipZh: 夸别人用 I really like / I love + your + 名词，对方的东西前要有 your。夸奖后常常接一个问题，比如 Where did you get it?，聊天就能继续下去。

title: 聊自己的爱好

options.en: Do you want to try it with me
Do you have any hobbies yourself
Would you like to join me sometime

examples.en: Actually, I've been really into hiking lately. Do you want to try it with me?
examples.zh: 其实，我最近特别迷徒步。你想跟我一起试试吗？

examples.en: Well, I've been really into photography lately. Have you ever tried it?
examples.zh: 嗯，我最近特别迷摄影。你试过吗？

examples.en: Honestly, I've been really into yoga lately. Would you like to join me sometime?
examples.zh: 说实话，我最近特别迷瑜伽。改天你想一起来吗？

tipZh: be into + 名词 / 动名词 = 迷上了……。I've been into … lately 表示“最近一直迷着”。说完后抛一个问题给对方，对话才不会冷场。
soundZh: into → in-too

title: 表示惊讶

options.en: you used to live in Paris

examples.en: Wow! I didn't know you could play the piano. That's so cool.
examples.zh: 哇！我不知道你会弹钢琴。太酷了。

examples.en: No way! I had no idea you used to live in Paris. You're full of surprises.
examples.zh: 不会吧！我完全不知道你以前住在巴黎。你真是深藏不露。

examples.en: Whoa! I never knew you had a twin sister. Tell me more.
examples.zh: 哇哦！我从来不知道你有个双胞胎姐妹。快多跟我说说。

tipZh: 表示惊讶：No way! / Wow! 开头，再用 I didn’t know / I had no idea 说“我之前不知道”，后面接完整句子。I never knew 语气更强。
soundZh: I didn't know → I didn' know；I had no idea → I-had-no-idea

title: 指认某个人

options.en: the woman in the red coat

examples.en: Oh, Anna is the one who lives next door to me.
examples.zh: 哦，安娜就是住在我隔壁的那个人。

examples.en: Actually, Mr. Lee is the one who knows everything about the city.
examples.zh: 其实，李先生就是对这座城市了如指掌的那个人。

examples.en: Yes, the woman in the red coat is the one who always makes everyone laugh.
examples.zh: 是的，穿红外套的那位女士就是总能把大家逗笑的那个人。

tipZh: the one who + 动词 用来说明“就是那个……的人”。who 在从句里当主语，所以后面的动词要跟着变：lives、sits、knows 都要加 -s。

title: 说自己的强项和弱项

examples.en: Reading is easy for me, but speaking is hard.
examples.zh: 阅读对我来说很容易，但口语很难。

examples.en: Grammar is fun for me, but pronunciation is tricky.
examples.zh: 语法对我来说很有意思，但发音有点棘手。

examples.en: Writing is pretty simple for me, but listening to fast speech is really difficult.
examples.zh: 写作对我来说挺简单，但听语速快的内容非常困难。

tipZh: “A 对我来说……，但 B ……”用 A is … for me, but B is …。for me 说明“对我而言”，放在形容词后面。speaking、pronunciation 这类做主语的名词不用加 the。

title: 请老师讲解区别

options.en: the difference between say and tell
options.zh: say 和 tell 的区别

options.en: the difference between make and do
options.zh: make 和 do 的区别

options.en: the difference between since and for
options.zh: since 和 for 的区别

options.en: the difference between much and many
options.zh: much 和 many 的区别

options.en: the difference between borrow and lend
options.zh: borrow 和 lend 的区别

examples.en: Sorry, could you explain the difference between say and tell again?
examples.zh: 不好意思，你能再解释一下 say 和 tell 的区别吗？

examples.en: Teacher, could you explain the difference between much and many with an example?
examples.zh: 老师，你能举个例子解释一下 much 和 many 的区别吗？

examples.en: Excuse me, could you explain the difference between borrow and lend in simple English?
examples.zh: 打扰一下，你能用简单的英语解释一下 borrow 和 lend 的区别吗？

tipZh: the difference between A and B = A 和 B 的区别。请对方换一种讲法，可以加 with an example（举个例子）或 in simple English（用简单的英语）。
soundZh: Could you → Couldja

title: 表达学习上的遗憾

options.zh: 跟外国人聊天时不慌张

options.en: I don't have enough time to practice
options.zh: 我没有足够的时间练习

examples.en: Honestly, I wish I could speak English more fluently, but I'm too shy.
examples.zh: 说实话，我真希望自己能把英语说得更流利，但我太害羞了。

examples.en: Sometimes, I wish I could give presentations in English, but I get nervous easily.
examples.zh: 有时候，我真希望自己能用英语做演讲，但我很容易紧张。

examples.en: Frankly, I wish I could chat with foreigners without panicking, but my vocabulary is too small.
examples.zh: 坦白说，我真希望自己能跟外国人聊天时不慌张，但我的词汇量太小了。

tipZh: I wish I could + 动词原形 表达“要是我能……就好了”（现实中做不到）。wish 后面的 could 是对现在的遗憾，不要用 can。后面的 but 说明原因。
soundZh: I wish I could → I-wish-I-cud

title: 道别并送上祝福

examples.en: It was great seeing you. Have a great weekend!
examples.zh: 很高兴见到你。祝你周末非常愉快！

examples.en: Thanks for stopping by. Have a wonderful evening!
examples.zh: 谢谢你过来坐坐。祝你晚上特别愉快！

examples.en: Good to see you. Have a lovely trip!
examples.zh: 见到你真好。祝你旅途很开心！

tipZh: 分别时先说一句感受，再用 “Have a + 形容词 + 名词” 送上祝福，母语者几乎每次告别都会说。
soundZh: Have a → Ha-va（连读）；talking to → talkin'-ta

title: 初次见面自我介绍

options.zh: 我在一家小创业公司上班

examples.en: Nice to meet you. I'm Anna, and I work in marketing.
examples.zh: 很高兴认识你。我是安娜，我在市场部工作。

examples.en: Good to meet you. I'm Linda, and I live just around the corner.
examples.zh: 很高兴见到你。我是琳达，我就住在附近。

examples.en: Pleased to meet you. I'm Wei, and I study design at the university.
examples.zh: 幸会。我是小伟，我在大学学设计。

tipZh: “Nice to meet you.” 之后马上用 “I'm + 名字, and I + 动词” 补一句自己的情况，对话就能自然往下走。
soundZh: Nice to meet you → Nice-ta meet-cha（meet you 连成 meetcha）

title: 欢迎新人
pattern: Welcome to {place}! Let me know if you need {thing} {tail}.
patternZh: 欢迎来到{place}！{tail}需要{thing}，告诉我一声。

examples.en: Welcome to the team! Let me know if you need anything at any time.
examples.zh: 欢迎来到团队！任何时候需要什么，告诉我一声。

examples.en: Welcome to the neighborhood! Let me know if you need some tips while you settle in.
examples.zh: 欢迎来到这个小区！安顿下来的这段时间需要一些建议，告诉我一声。

examples.en: Welcome to the family! Let me know if you need directions during your first week.
examples.zh: 欢迎来到这个大家庭！头一周需要问路，告诉我一声。

tipZh: 迎接新同事、新邻居时，先说 Welcome to …，再补一句 Let me know if you need … 表示愿意帮忙。
soundZh: Let me know → Lemme know；Welcome to → Welcum-ta

title: 回应对方讲的事

options.en: How do you feel about it

examples.en: Oh, that sounds great. How did it go?
examples.zh: 哦，听起来很棒。后来怎么样了？

examples.en: Wow, that sounds exhausting. What happened next?
examples.zh: 哇，听起来很累人。接下来发生了什么？

examples.en: Honestly, that sounds interesting. What did you do?
examples.zh: 说实话，听起来很有意思。你当时怎么办的？

tipZh: 听完别人讲经历，先用 That sounds + 形容词 表态，再追问一句，对话就不会冷场。
soundZh: sounds → 句中 d 常被吞掉，听起来像 “sounz”；that sounds → thatsounz

title: 感叹式回应

examples.en: Oh, what a great idea!
examples.zh: 哦，真是很棒的主意！

examples.en: Wow, what a nice surprise!
examples.zh: 哇，真是不错的惊喜！

examples.en: Honestly, what a terrific gift!
examples.zh: 说真的，真是极好的礼物！

tipZh: “What a + 形容词 + 名词!” 是最常用的感叹回应，注意一定要带 a，名词用单数。
soundZh: What a → Whadda（连读成 Whadda）

title: 听到好消息的回应

examples.en: Oh, that's great to hear. I'm really happy for you.
examples.zh: 哦，听到这个消息太好了。我真心替你高兴。

examples.en: Well, that's wonderful to hear. You deserve it.
examples.zh: 嗯，听到这个消息太棒了。这是你应得的。

examples.en: Wow, that's nice to hear. Keep up the good work.
examples.zh: 哇，听到这个消息真不错。继续保持。

tipZh: 别人告诉你好消息时说 That's great to hear，后面再补一句祝贺，比单说 Good 热情得多。
soundZh: That's great to hear → Thats-great-ta hear；to 弱读成 ta

title: 争取时间再回复
pattern: {opener} let me {action} first. I'll get back to you {time}.

options.en: by the end of the week

examples.en: Hmm, let me check my calendar first. I'll get back to you this afternoon.
examples.zh: 嗯，我先看一下我的日程，今天下午再回复你。

examples.en: Okay, let me talk to my team first. I'll get back to you later today.
examples.zh: 好的，我先跟团队商量一下，今天晚些时候再回复你。

examples.en: Sure, let me double-check the numbers first. I'll get back to you in a few minutes.
examples.zh: 当然，我先再核对一下数字，几分钟后再回复你。

tipZh: 被问到当场答不了的事，不要硬撑，先用 Let me … first 争取时间，再给出明确的回复时间。
soundZh: Let me → Lemme；get back to → get-back-ta

title: 被问住时拖延一下

options.en: think about that for a second
figure out how to explain it

examples.en: Hmm, that's a good question. Let me think.
examples.zh: 嗯，这是个好问题。让我想想。

examples.en: Well, that's a great question. Let me think about that for a second.
examples.zh: 嗯，这是个很棒的问题。让我想一下。

examples.en: You know, that's a hard question. Let me get this right.
examples.zh: 这个嘛，这是个棘手的问题。让我把话说准确。

tipZh: 被问到不好回答的问题，先说 That's a good question 夸一句，再说 Let me think，自然地争取思考时间。
soundZh: that's a → thatsa；Let me → Lemme

title: 先肯定再转折

options.en: I'm a little worried about the cost
I'd like to see more details first
I'd want to think about it more
I'd compare it with other options
options.zh: 我会再和别的选择比较一下

examples.en: The new phone looks great on paper. That said, I'm a little worried about the cost.
examples.zh: 新手机纸面上看很不错。话是这么说，我有点担心费用。

examples.en: Her plan works for me. On the other hand, I'm not completely sure yet.
examples.zh: 她的计划我这边没问题。不过另一方面，我还不完全确定。

examples.en: His idea looks promising. Having said that, I'd compare it with other options.
examples.zh: 他的想法看起来很有希望。尽管如此，我会再和别的选择比较一下。

tipZh: 先说优点，再用 That said / On the other hand 转折提出顾虑，既礼貌又清楚，是做判断时的常用组织方式。
soundZh: On the other hand → On-the-other-hand 连读很快；Having said that → Havin' said that

title: 用 Speaking of 转换话题

options.en: have a funny story about that

options.zh: 看到过一些很有意思的内容

options.en: have a quick question for you

examples.en: Oh, speaking of food, I have a funny story about that.
examples.zh: 哦，说到吃的，我有个好笑的故事。

examples.en: Hey, speaking of movies, I have a quick question for you.
examples.zh: 嘿，说到电影，我有个小问题想问你。

examples.en: Wait, speaking of work, I have a good idea.
examples.zh: 等等，说到工作，我有个好主意。

tipZh: 别人提到相关的话题时，用 Speaking of … 顺势把话题接到自己想说的事上，听起来很自然。
soundZh: Speaking of → Speakin'-ov

title: 列举两条理由

options.en: the office is close to home
I get to learn a lot

examples.en: To start with, the team is great. On top of that, the pay is decent.
examples.zh: 首先，团队很棒。除此之外，薪水还不错。

examples.en: For one thing, the office is close to home. Besides, the commute is short.
examples.zh: 一方面，办公室离家很近。再说，通勤时间很短。

examples.en: Well, for starters, the work is interesting. Also, my manager is supportive.
examples.zh: 嗯，先说一点，工作很有意思。另外，我的主管很支持我。

tipZh: 解释原因时，用 To start with … 加 On top of that … 把理由一条一条排开，逻辑清楚，也给自己争取了思考时间。
soundZh: On top of that → On-top-ov-that

title: 说出自己不太喜欢什么
pattern: {opener} I'm not a big fan of {thing}, {tail}.

examples.en: Well, I'm not a big fan of spicy food, to be honest.
examples.zh: 嗯，说实话，我不太喜欢辛辣食物。

examples.en: Actually, I'm not a big fan of crowded places, in general.
examples.zh: 其实，总的来说，我不太喜欢人多的地方。

examples.en: Personally, I'm not a big fan of small talk, if I'm being honest.
examples.zh: 就我个人而言，老实讲，我不太喜欢闲聊。

tipZh: I'm not a big fan of … 比 I don't like … 委婉得多，说不喜欢某样东西时母语者更常用它。
soundZh: a big fan of → a-big-fan-ov

title: 要我说……

examples.en: Honestly, if you ask me, that movie is overrated.
examples.zh: 说实话，要我说，那部电影被高估了。

examples.en: Well, if you ask me, this app is a bit overpriced.
examples.zh: 嗯，要我说，这个应用有点贵了。

examples.en: Look, if you ask me, that restaurant is better than it looks.
examples.zh: 听我说，要我说，那家餐厅比看上去要好。

tipZh: If you ask me, … 用来亮出自己的看法，语气随意，不带攻击性，朋友之间闲聊很常用。
soundZh: If you ask me → If-ya-ask-me

title: 就某一方面表态

examples.en: Well, as far as the schedule goes, I think it's fine.
examples.zh: 嗯，至于时间安排，我觉得没问题。

examples.en: Honestly, as far as the food goes, I have a few concerns.
examples.zh: 说实话，至于食物，我有几点担心。

examples.en: Personally, as far as the price goes, I'm not sure yet.
examples.zh: 就我个人而言，至于价格，我还不确定。

tipZh: As far as … goes 先点明你要评价的方面，再给看法，适合逐项反馈（时间、预算、地点等）。
soundZh: as far as → as-far-az

title: 看情况再决定

examples.en: Well, it depends on the weather, but I'd go for it.
examples.zh: 嗯，这要看天气，不过我会去试试。

examples.en: Honestly, it depends on how much time you have, but I'm leaning towards no.
examples.zh: 说实话，这要看你有多少时间，不过我倾向于不去。

examples.en: Hmm, it depends on what you like, but I'd wait a little.
examples.zh: 嗯，这要看你喜欢什么，不过我会再等等。

tipZh: 被问 “要不要……” 时，用 It depends on … 说明条件，再补一句自己的倾向，比直接回答 Yes/No 更真实。
soundZh: depends on → depen(d)s-on；I mean → I-mean

title: 说最喜欢的一点
pattern: {opener} what I like most about {place} is {thing}.

examples.en: Honestly, what I like most about this city is the people.
examples.zh: 说实话，我最喜欢这座城市的人。

examples.en: Well, what I like most about this restaurant is the location.
examples.zh: 嗯，我最喜欢这家餐厅的位置。

examples.en: Actually, what I like most about this place is the view.
examples.zh: 其实，我最喜欢这个地方的景色。

tipZh: What I like most about … is … 是 “我最喜欢……的是……” 的整块句型，is 后面直接接名词，不要多加 that。
soundZh: What I like → Whadai-like

title: 表明同意的程度

examples.en: I totally agree with you about the schedule.
examples.zh: 关于时间安排，我完全同意你的看法。

examples.en: I mostly agree with Anna about the timing.
examples.zh: 关于时机，我基本上同意安娜的看法。

examples.en: I can't fully agree with Tom about that.
examples.zh: 关于这件事，我不能完全同意汤姆的看法。

tipZh: 表示同意用 agree with + 人，不用 agree you；程度副词放在 agree 前面，可以从 totally 一直调到 don't really。
soundZh: agree with → agree-with；don't really → doan-really

title: 委婉地质疑

options.en: I hate to say it, but

examples.en: Hmm, I'm not sure that's a good idea right now.
examples.zh: 嗯，我不确定现在这样做是个好主意。

examples.en: Honestly, I'm not sure that's realistic in this case.
examples.zh: 说实话，我不确定在这种情况下这样做现实。

examples.en: I hate to say it, but I'm not sure that's the best way at this point.
examples.zh: 我不想这么说，但是我不确定到这个阶段这样做是最好的办法。

tipZh: 直接说 No 太硬，I'm not sure that's … 把反对说成 “我不确定”，在职场和朋友间都很安全。
soundZh: I'm not sure that's → I'm not-shur thats

title: 支持或不太支持某个想法

examples.en: I'm all for working from home right now.
examples.zh: 现在，我非常赞成在家办公。

examples.en: I'm in favor of starting earlier this time.
examples.zh: 这一次，我赞同早点开始。

examples.en: I'm not sure about saving more money for the team.
examples.zh: 为了团队，我不太确定要不要多存点钱。

tipZh: 这几个表态短语后面都接 -ing 形式（名词性），不接动词原形；从 all for 到 not sure about 表示支持程度的变化。
soundZh: I'm all for → I'm-all-fer

title: 我的看法稍有不同

options.en: but I get where you're coming from

examples.en: Well, I see it a bit differently, I think.
examples.zh: 嗯，我对这件事的看法稍有不同，我觉得。

examples.en: Hmm, I see the schedule a bit differently, but that's just me.
examples.zh: 嗯，我对时间安排的看法稍有不同，不过这只是我的看法。

examples.en: Honestly, I see the risks a bit differently, but I get where you're coming from.
examples.zh: 说实话，我对风险的看法稍有不同，不过我理解你的想法。

tipZh: I see it a bit differently 是不同意时最常用的缓冲说法，比 I disagree 温和，后面通常还会接自己的理由。
soundZh: a bit → a-bit（t 轻读）；where you're coming from → where-ya-comin'-from

title: 礼貌地表示不能同意

options.en: I hate to say it, but

examples.en: Sorry, but I can't really agree with that right now.
examples.zh: 抱歉，不过现在我不太能同意这个说法。

examples.en: I hate to say it, but I can't really agree with the second point at this stage.
examples.zh: 我不想这么说，不过现阶段我不太能同意第二点。

examples.en: I'm afraid I can't really agree with the whole idea for now.
examples.zh: 恐怕目前我不太能同意整个想法。

tipZh: 想拒绝对方观点时，先用 Sorry, but / I'm afraid 缓冲，再说 I can't really agree，语气会柔和很多。
soundZh: can't really agree → can't-really-agree（t 吞音）；I'm afraid I → I'm-afraid-I

title: 真诚道歉并补救

options.en: Let me make it up to you
I'll make sure it's sorted out

examples.en: Hey, I'm so sorry for the mix-up. It won't happen again.
examples.zh: 嘿，我为这次弄混了真的很抱歉。以后不会再发生了。

examples.en: Look, I'm so sorry for the confusion. Let me make it up to you.
examples.zh: 听我说，我为造成的困惑真的很抱歉。让我来补偿你。

examples.en: Ah, I'm so sorry for the mess. I'll make sure it's sorted out.
examples.zh: 啊，我为弄得一团糟真的很抱歉。我会确保把它处理好。

tipZh: 道歉用 sorry for + 名词/动名词，后面马上补一句补救办法，比反复说 sorry 更有诚意。
soundZh: so sorry for → so-sorry-fer；make it up to you → make-it-up-ta-ya

title: 郑重地表示感谢

examples.en: Today, I really appreciate your help.
examples.zh: 今天，我真的感谢你的帮助。

examples.en: This week, I truly appreciate your advice.
examples.zh: 这周，我由衷地感谢你的建议。

examples.en: Once again, I genuinely appreciate the invitation.
examples.zh: 再一次，我发自内心地感谢你的邀请。

tipZh: appreciate 后面直接接被感谢的事物（your help），不接人；比 thank you 更郑重，适合邮件和工作场合。
soundZh: appreciate → a-PRE-shee-ate

title: 别人道谢后的回应

options.en: Let me know if you need anything else
options.zh: 还需要什么尽管告诉我

options.en: It was no trouble at all
Call me if it happens again
options.zh: 要是再发生就给我打电话

examples.en: Oh, no problem. Let me know if you need anything else.
examples.zh: 哦，没问题。还需要什么尽管告诉我。

examples.en: Hey, anytime. I'm glad it worked out.
examples.zh: 嘿，随时都行。很高兴事情解决了。

examples.en: Of course, my pleasure. Call me if it happens again.
examples.zh: 当然，这是我的荣幸。要是再发生就给我打电话。

tipZh: 别人说 Thank you 之后，只回 You're welcome 略显单调；换成 No problem / Anytime，再补半句，对话更自然。
soundZh: Happy to → Happy-ta；Don't mention it → Doan-mention-it

title: 请对方再说一遍

options.en: if it's not too much trouble

examples.en: Sorry, if possible, could you say that again?
examples.zh: 抱歉，可以的话，能请你再说一遍吗？

examples.en: Excuse me, if you don't mind, could you speak a little slower?
examples.zh: 不好意思，如果你不介意，能请你说慢一点吗？

examples.en: Hmm, if it's not too much trouble, could you spell that for me?
examples.zh: 嗯，如果不太麻烦，能请你帮我拼一下吗？

tipZh: 没听清时别只说 What?，用 Could you say that again? 加上礼貌语，在电话和会议里都合适。
soundZh: Could you → Couldja；say that again → say-that-agen

title: 问对方这话是什么意思

options.en: what exactly do you mean by
so what do you mean by

examples.en: Sorry, what do you mean by that?
examples.zh: 抱歉，你说的那个是什么意思？

examples.en: Wait, what exactly do you mean by a soft launch?
examples.zh: 等等，你具体说的软启动是什么意思？

examples.en: Hmm, so what do you mean by a quick fix?
examples.zh: 嗯，那你说的应急方案是什么意思？

tipZh: 听到没听懂的词或说法，用 What do you mean by … 直接问，by 后面接名词或 that，不要接完整句子。
soundZh: What do you mean → Whaddya mean；What did you → Whadidja

title: 确认是哪一个

options.zh: 这个周五还是下个周五

options.en: the first draft or the final draft
the old version or the new one
I just want to be sure
I don't want to mix things up
I want to get it right
I'd hate to get it wrong

examples.en: Sorry, do you mean this Friday or next Friday? I just want to be sure.
examples.zh: 抱歉，你是指这个周五还是下个周五？我只是想确认一下。

examples.en: Wait, do you mean the first draft or the final draft? I want to get it right.
examples.zh: 等等，你是指初稿还是终稿？我想弄清楚。

examples.en: Just to be clear, do you mean Tom or Tim? I'd hate to get it wrong.
examples.zh: 我确认一下，你是指汤姆还是蒂姆？我可不想搞错。

tipZh: 容易混淆时，直接把两个选项放进 Do you mean A or B? 里确认，比猜错再改要省事得多。
soundZh: do you mean → dya mean

title: 说出期待的事

examples.en: Honestly, I'm really looking forward to the weekend.
examples.zh: 说实话，我非常期待周末。

examples.en: Actually, we're really looking forward to the trip.
examples.zh: 其实，我们非常期待这次旅行。

examples.en: Well, they're really looking forward to meeting your family.
examples.zh: 嗯，他们非常期待见你的家人。

tipZh: look forward to 里的 to 是介词，后面接名词或 -ing，不接动词原形：looking forward to seeing you，不是 to see。
soundZh: looking forward to → lookin' forward ta

title: 难以置信的惊讶

examples.en: Wow, I can't believe it's already Friday! That's crazy.
examples.zh: 哇，我真不敢相信已经周五了！太疯狂了。

examples.en: Oh my gosh, I can't believe you remembered! I need a minute.
examples.zh: 天哪，我真不敢相信你居然还记得！让我缓一下。

examples.en: Honestly, I can't believe we actually won! Give me a second.
examples.zh: 老实说，我真不敢相信我们居然赢了！让我静一静。

tipZh: I can't believe + 从句 表示惊讶，后面可以接整句，也可以接 how + 形容词；惊讶的内容不一定是坏事。
soundZh: can't believe → can't-beleev（t 吞音）

title: 说什么让我有某种感受

examples.en: These days, loud noise makes me nervous.
examples.zh: 最近，噪音太大让我紧张。

examples.en: Lately, long meetings make me anxious.
examples.zh: 这阵子，开长会让我焦虑。

examples.en: At the moment, public speaking makes me tired.
examples.zh: 眼下，当众演讲让我疲惫。

tipZh: make + 人 + 形容词 是表达 “某事让我觉得……” 的固定用法；主语是复数名词时动词用 make，单数用 makes。
soundZh: makes me → mak-sme

title: 庆幸与松一口气

examples.en: I'm so glad that it's over.
examples.zh: 我真是高兴，终于结束了。

examples.en: We're so relieved that everything worked out.
examples.zh: 我们真是松了口气，一切都顺利解决了。

examples.en: They're so thankful that it's Friday.
examples.zh: 他们真是感激，今天是周五。

tipZh: so + 形容词 + that + 从句 说明让你高兴或松气的原因；口语里 that 常常省略。
soundZh: so glad → so-glad；that 在句中常弱读成 /ðət/，甚至省略

title: 给出温和的建议

examples.en: Honestly, you should take a break first.
examples.zh: 说实话，你应该先休息一下。

examples.en: Look, you could talk to someone this week.
examples.zh: 听我说，你可以这周找人聊聊。

examples.en: Maybe you ought to double-check the address soon.
examples.zh: 也许你应该尽快仔细核对地址。

tipZh: should 语气较直接，might want to / could 更委婉；modal 后面都接动词原形，不加 to（ought to 除外）。
soundZh: should → shud；ought to → otta；might want to → might-wanna

title: 提醒别忘了某事

examples.en: Hey, don't forget to bring your ID before you leave.
examples.zh: 嘿，出门前别忘了带上身份证。

examples.en: Also, make sure you charge your phone tomorrow morning.
examples.zh: 还有，明天早上一定要给手机充电。

examples.en: By the way, be sure to check the weather this weekend.
examples.zh: 顺便说一下，这个周末务必看一下天气。

tipZh: Don't forget to / Remember to / Make sure you / Be sure to 都后接动词原形，是日常提醒别人最常用的四种说法。
soundZh: don't forget to → doan-forgetta；make sure you → make-shur-ya

title: 提醒小心别弄丢东西

examples.en: Hey, be careful not to lose your passport at the airport.
examples.zh: 嘿，在机场小心别弄丢护照。

examples.en: Remember, try not to drop your wallet on the train.
examples.zh: 记住，在火车上尽量别摔了钱包。

examples.en: Also, be sure not to forget your phone at the hotel.
examples.zh: 还有，在酒店注意别忘了拿手机。

tipZh: “提醒别做某事” 要把 not 放在 to 前面：be careful not to lose，不是 be careful to not lose 或 don't to lose。
soundZh: careful not to → careful-nah-ta；try not to → try-nah-ta

title: 稳妥起见的小建议

options.en: It might be a good idea to

examples.en: It might be a good idea to double-check the details just in case.
examples.zh: 以防万一，不妨再核对一下细节。

examples.en: It's probably best to leave a bit earlier this time.
examples.zh: 这一次，最好早点出发。

examples.en: It'd be better to bring a jacket before the weekend.
examples.zh: 周末之前，最稳妥的做法是带件外套。

tipZh: 这四个开头都是 “稍微有点建议” 的软性说法，后面统一接动词原形；比直接用 You should 礼貌，不容易让人觉得被命令。
soundZh: might be a → might-be-a；probably → prolly

title: 鼓励对方

examples.en: Don't worry, I'm sure you'll do great this time.
examples.zh: 别担心，我相信你这次会做得很好。

examples.en: Relax, I'm sure you'll figure it out in the end.
examples.zh: 放松，我相信你最后能想明白。

examples.en: Come on, I'm sure you'll manage with a little practice.
examples.zh: 加油，我相信你多练习一下就能应付。

tipZh: I'm sure you'll + 动词原形 是鼓励别人最万能的句式，前面加 Don't worry 或 Hang in there 语气更温暖。
soundZh: I'm sure you'll → I'm-shur-yool

title: 我好像做不到

examples.en: Sorry, I can't seem to get a signal today.
examples.zh: 抱歉，今天我好像没法收到信号。

examples.en: Hmm, I can't seem to log in at the moment.
examples.zh: 嗯，眼下我好像没法登录。

examples.en: Honestly, I can't seem to focus for some reason.
examples.zh: 说实话，不知为什么我好像没法集中精神。

tipZh: I can't seem to … 表示 “怎么也……不了”，比 I can't 更口语，带点无奈，抱怨小问题时很常用。
soundZh: can't seem to → can't-seem-ta

title: 反映东西和预期不符

options.en: Could I speak to the manager

examples.en: Excuse me, this isn't what I expected. Could you take a look?
examples.zh: 不好意思，这个和我预期的不一样。能帮我看一下吗？

examples.en: Sorry, the room isn't what we agreed on. Could you fix it?
examples.zh: 抱歉，这个房间和我们约定的不一样。能帮我处理一下吗？

examples.en: Um, the item isn't what the picture showed. Could I speak to the manager?
examples.zh: 呃，这件商品和图片上显示的不一样。能让我和经理谈谈吗？

tipZh: 收到不对的东西时，先客观说 this isn't what I expected，再提出明确的请求，比直接抱怨更容易解决问题。
soundZh: isn't what → isn't-what；Could I → Could-dai

title: 东西用完了想借或买

options.en: Do you have any to spare
Do you know where I can get more

examples.en: Hey, I've run out of cash. Do you have any to spare?
examples.zh: 嘿，我的现金用完了。你有多余的吗？

examples.en: Sorry, I've run out of printer paper. Could I borrow some?
examples.zh: 抱歉，我的打印纸用完了。我能借一点吗？

examples.en: Excuse me, I've run out of laundry detergent. Is there a store nearby?
examples.zh: 不好意思，我的洗衣液用完了。附近有商店吗？

tipZh: run out of 表示 “用完了”，后面接不可数名词最自然；紧接着提出请求，别人就知道你想要什么帮助。
soundZh: run out of → run-out-ov；I've → Ive

title: 讲第一次的经历

options.en: had no idea what I was doing
options.zh: 完全不知道自己在干什么

options.en: but I got used to it
and I still laugh about it
options.zh: 现在想起来还觉得好笑

examples.en: The first time I tried sushi, I was really nervous, but I got used to it.
examples.zh: 我第一次吃寿司的时候，特别紧张，不过后来就习惯了。

examples.en: The first time I flew alone, I couldn't stop laughing, and I still remember it.
examples.zh: 我第一次一个人坐飞机的时候，笑得停不下来，到现在还记得。

examples.en: The first time I moved abroad, I thought I'd mess up, and I still laugh about it.
examples.zh: 我第一次搬到国外的时候，怕自己搞砸，现在想起来还觉得好笑。

tipZh: The first time I + 过去式 是讲 “第一次……的时候” 的万能开头，后面接当时的感受，再补一句后来怎么样。
soundZh: The first time I → The first-time-I；had no idea → had-no-idea

title: 说自己去过哪里

options.en: and I'd go back in a heartbeat
but I'd like to see more
but I'd love to go back

examples.en: I've been to Japan once, and I loved it.
examples.zh: 日本我去过一次，而且我很喜欢。

examples.en: I've been to Paris a few times, but I'd like to see more.
examples.zh: 巴黎我去过好几次，不过我还想多看看。

examples.en: I've been to Bali many times, but I'd love to go back.
examples.zh: 巴厘岛我去过很多次，不过我还想再去。

tipZh: have been to 表示 “去过（并已回来）”，和 have gone to（去了还没回来）不同；次数放在地点后面。
soundZh: I've been to → I've-bin-ta（been 弱读成 bin）

title: 讲事情最后怎么收场

examples.en: Long story short, I ended up staying home after all that.
examples.zh: 长话短说，我折腾了一通，最后留在家里。

examples.en: Anyway, we ended up ordering pizza because of the rain.
examples.zh: 总之，我们因为下雨，最后点了披萨。

examples.en: So, they ended up missing the train as usual.
examples.zh: 所以，他们一如既往，最后错过了火车。

tipZh: end up + -ing 表示 “结果……了、最后落得……”，通常是事先没打算好的结局；up 后面接动名词，不接 to。
soundZh: ended up → endid-up（连读）

title: 有点怪但还不错

options.en: if you like that kind of thing
options.zh: 如果你喜欢那种风格的话

examples.en: This place is kind of weird, but in a good way.
examples.zh: 这个地方有点怪，不过是好的那种。

examples.en: Her style is kind of chaotic, if you like that kind of thing.
examples.zh: 她的风格有点混乱，如果你喜欢那种风格的话。

examples.en: His sense of humor is kind of strange, but I like it.
examples.zh: 他的幽默感有点奇特，不过我挺喜欢。

tipZh: kind of 放在形容词前面表示 “有点”，语气比 a bit 更随意，后面常接 but 补一个正面评价。
soundZh: kind of → kinda；is kind of → is-kinda

title: 欢迎对方随时找你

examples.en: Sure, feel free to call me any time.
examples.zh: 当然可以，任何时候尽管打电话给我。

examples.en: Of course, feel free to drop by whenever you like.
examples.zh: 没问题，你什么时候想尽管过来坐坐。

examples.en: Absolutely, feel free to borrow my notes if it helps.
examples.zh: 当然，如果有帮助的话尽管借我的笔记。

tipZh: Feel free to + 动词原形 是 “别客气，想……就……” 的主动邀请，比 You can 更友好。
soundZh: feel free to → feel-free-ta

title: 提议一起做点什么

examples.en: I was thinking we could grab lunch on Friday. What do you think?
examples.zh: 我在想我们周五可以吃个午饭。你觉得怎么样？

examples.en: I was thinking we could see a movie after work. Does that work for you?
examples.zh: 我在想我们下班后可以看场电影。你方便吗？

examples.en: I was thinking we could catch up over coffee sometime next week. How does that sound?
examples.zh: 我在想我们下周找个时间可以喝杯咖啡叙叙旧。听起来怎么样？

tipZh: I was thinking we could … 用过去进行时把提议说得很随意，对方拒绝也不尴尬；最后记得加一句征求意见。
soundZh: was thinking → wuz thinkin'；we could → we-cud

title: 爽快地接受邀请

examples.en: Oh, sure, I'd love to. What time should I come?
examples.zh: 哦，好啊，我很乐意。我几点到？

examples.en: Hey, yeah, count me in. Should I bring anything?
examples.zh: 嘿，没问题，算我一个。需要我带什么吗？

examples.en: Oh nice, that sounds great, I'm in. Who else is coming?
examples.zh: 哇，听起来很棒，我加入。还有谁会来？

tipZh: 接受邀请时，先爽快答应，再顺手问一个细节（时间、地点、要带什么），显得积极又靠谱。
soundZh: count me in → count-me-in；I'd love to → I'd-love-ta

title: 请教最好的办法

examples.en: Sorry, what's the best way to get downtown, in your experience?
examples.zh: 抱歉，根据你的经验，去市中心的最好办法是什么？

examples.en: Quick question, what's the best way to stay focused, in your opinion?
examples.zh: 问一下，在你看来，保持专注的最好办法是什么？

examples.en: Excuse me, what's the best way to cook rice, from your point of view?
examples.zh: 不好意思，从你的角度来看，煮米饭的最好办法是什么？

tipZh: What's the best way to + 动词原形 是请教方法的万能问法，后面不要再加 for。
soundZh: What's the best way to → Whats-the-bes-way-ta（best 的 t 常吞掉）

title: 问对方做了多久

examples.en: So, how long have you lived here? Do you enjoy it?
examples.zh: 那，你住在这里多久了？你喜欢吗？

examples.en: By the way, how long have you been playing the guitar? Was it hard at first?
examples.zh: 顺便问一下，你弹吉他多久了？一开始难吗？

examples.en: Just curious, how long have you had that car? Is it what you expected?
examples.zh: 随便问问，你有那辆车多久了？和你想的一样吗？

tipZh: How long have you + 过去分词 问的是 “从过去到现在持续了多久”，别用一般过去时 How long did you。
soundZh: how long have you → how-long-hav-ya；Out of curiosity → Out-ov-curiosity

title: 问对方有什么安排
pattern: {opener} do you have any plans for {time}? {follow}.

options.en: A few of us are going out

examples.en: Hey, do you have any plans for the weekend? We should catch up.
examples.zh: 嘿，周末你有什么安排吗？我们应该聚聚。

examples.en: So, do you have any plans for the holidays? A few of us are going out.
examples.zh: 那，假期你有什么安排吗？我们几个人要出去。

examples.en: Just curious, do you have any plans for your birthday? I'm free if you are.
examples.zh: 随便问问，生日那天你有什么安排吗？只要你有空我就有空。

tipZh: 想约人但还没开口时，先问 Do you have any plans for …，对方有空自然会接话，没空也不会尴尬。
soundZh: Do you have any → Dya have any

title: 打听别人的八卦

options.en: Do you know anything about it

examples.en: Oh, I heard Anna got a new job. Is that true?
examples.zh: 哦，我听说安娜找到了新工作。是真的吗？

examples.en: Hey, I heard your sister is getting married. Is that right?
examples.zh: 嘿，我听说你姐姐要结婚了。对吗？

examples.en: Wait, I heard the new guy had a baby. Do you know anything about it?
examples.zh: 等等，我听说新来的那个人生孩子了。你知道什么内幕吗？

tipZh: I heard + 从句（that 可省略）用来转述听来的消息，后面接 Is that true? 向对方求证，语气好奇而不武断。
soundZh: I heard → I-heard（d 轻读）；Is that → Izzat
